# Differential analysis using Coefficient-based approach

In the reference analysis, we introduced contrast-based approach. In this supplementary section, we introduce how to use coefficient-based model.

## Load data

We use the full dataset for this analysis. Same process here as in the reference analysis

```{r}
se <- readRDS("./datasets/whole_vHC_dataset.rds")
dge <- DGEList(assay(se, "counts"))
mm <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group, data=as.data.frame(colData(se)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
# Filter lowly expressed genes
keep <- filterByExpr(dge, mm, min.count = 10)
se <- se[keep, ]

# First we use SVA correction to capture latent technical variation
# There are two embedded methods to estimate the number of SVs: BE and LEEK
# We take a look at both of their estimation
set.seed(1)
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se, ~ 0 + group, numSVmethod = "be", method = "vst")
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se, ~ 0 + group, numSVmethod = "leek", method = "vst")
# we use 6 SVs as "BE" suggested
se <- SEtools::svacor(se, ~ 0 + group, n.sv = 6, method = "vst")
se <- log2FC(se, "corrected", controls = grep("Ctrl", se$group))  # calculate logFC relative to the mean of control samples
```

## DEA

```{r}
levels(se$Sex)
```

In this case, we use Male as reference level.

```{r}
formula <- paste(grep("^SV[0-9]", colnames(colData(se)), value = TRUE), collapse = "+")
formula <- as.formula(paste0("~", formula, "+Sex*Condition"))

mm <- model.matrix(formula, data = as.data.frame(colData(se)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(assay(se)))
dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm)
fit <- glmQLFit(dge, mm, prior.count=0.5)

Results_stress <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, grep("Condition", colnames(mm), value=TRUE)), Inf)) 
# Results_stress selects both ConditionStress and SexFemale:ConditionStress
# Answering the question: does Stress matter at all, either as a "main" effect or through its interaction with Sex

Results <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, grep("Condition|Sex", colnames(mm), value=TRUE)), Inf))
# Answering the question: does anything related to Condition or Sex matter

Results_sex <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, "SexFemale"), Inf))
# Results_sex only selects SexFemale
# Answering the question: is there any Sex difference specifically at the Condition reference level (Ctrl)

Results_interaction <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, "SexFemale:ConditionStress"), Inf)))
# Results_interaction only tests the interaction of Sex and Condition
# Answering the question: does the Stress effect differs between sexes

Results_M <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, "ConditionStress"),Inf))) 
# Results_M selects "ConditionStress"
# Answering the question: is there any Stress effect in males (because male is the reference sex)

M_signif <- rownames(Results_M[Results_M$FDR < 0.05, ])

# stageR
# Here we first try to use the pvalue from All Results as the input of screening
pScreen <- Results$PValue
names(pScreen) <- rownames(Results)
pConfirmation <- cbind(Interaction = Results_interaction[row.names(Results),"PValue"])
stageRObj <- stageR(pScreen = pScreen, pConfirmation = pConfirmation, pScreenAdjusted = FALSE)
stageRObj <- stageWiseAdjustment(object = stageRObj, method = "none", alpha = 0.05)
adj_PVals <- getAdjustedPValues(stageRObj, onlySignificantGenes = FALSE, order = FALSE) #returns NA for non-significant gene in pScreen
adj_PVals <- as.data.frame(adj_PVals)
Results_interaction$staged.FDR <- adj_PVals[rownames(Results_interaction),]$"Interaction"

intDEGs <- rownames(na.omit(Results_interaction[Results_interaction$staged.FDR < 0.05, ]))
intDEGs
```

```{r}
# To get the Stress effect in Females, the easiest way is to change the reference sex to Male from the very beginning, and run the test again
# We do this now for later use
se_femaleRef <- se
se_femaleRef$Sex <- relevel(se_femaleRef$Sex, ref = "Female")
mm_femaleRef <- model.matrix(formula, data = as.data.frame(colData(se_femaleRef)))
dge_femaleRef <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(assay(se_femaleRef)))
dge_femaleRef <- estimateDisp(dge_femaleRef, mm_femaleRef)
fit_femaleRef <- glmQLFit(dge_femaleRef, mm_femaleRef, prior.count = 0.5)
Results_F <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit_femaleRef, "ConditionStress"),Inf))) 
# Answering the question: is there any Stress effect in females (becase now female is the reference sex)
F_signif <- rownames(Results_F[Results_F$FDR < 0.05, ])
```

## A. Volcano plot of interaction genes

Use volcano plot to show the interaction results.

```{r}
show <- row.names(Results_interaction)[which(Results_interaction$staged.FDR < 0.015 & abs(Results_interaction$logFC) > 0.25)]      
sup_fig_coef_a <- volcano(Results_interaction, logFC = logFC, signif = staged.FDR, labels = show) + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.1,4.09)) + labs(x = "Sex:Stress Interaction logFC")
sup_fig_coef_a
```

## B. Heatmap of interaction genes

Use heatmap to show the interaction results.

```{r}
sup_fig_coef_b <- sechm(
  se = se, 
  feature = intDEGs,
  gaps_at = "Condition", 
  assayName = "corrected", 
  top_annotation = c("Condition", "Sex"),
  anno_labels = TRUE, 
  anno_label_gp = list(size = 8, col = "white"),
  do.scale = TRUE, 
  name = "z-score", 
  show_rownames = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE, 
  show_row_dend = FALSE,
  breaks = 0.98,
  column_title = NULL,
  use_raster = TRUE  
)
sup_fig_coef_b
```

## C. The correlation of interaction logFC and baseline logFC between sexes

```{r}
Results_interaction$logFC.Sex <- Results_sex[row.names(Results_interaction), "logFC"]
Results_interaction$logFC.stressMales <- Results_M[row.names(Results_interaction), "logFC"] 

Results_interaction2 <- Results_interaction[which(Results_interaction$staged.FDR < 0.15 & abs(Results_interaction$logFC) > 0.1),]
ct <- cor.test(Results_interaction2$logFC, Results_interaction2$logFC.Sex)
sup_fig_coef_c <- ggplot(Results_interaction2, aes(logFC.Sex, logFC)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ 0 + x, method = "lm") + 
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Baseline logFC between sexes", y = "Sex:Stress interaction logFC") +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = paste0(" R=", round(ct$estimate,2)," ***\n"), hjust = 0, vjust = 0)
sup_fig_coef_c
```

## Improved stageR Strategy

When we use the All Results to do FDR correction, there are a lot of genes that are driven by baseline sex difference but the stress effect of them are not obvious. So in the next chunk, we only use stress-relevan contrasts in screening, so that the screening is more targeted increases power

```{r}
# use stagedFDR to boost power for Sex*Stress (interaction term)
# Here we use everything except for Male.vs.Female as the screening model
Results_Screen2 <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, grep("Condition", colnames(mm), value=TRUE)), Inf))
pScreen2 <- Results_Screen2$PValue
names(pScreen2) <- rownames(Results_Screen2)
pConfirmation2 <- cbind(Interaction = Results_interaction[row.names(Results_Screen2),"PValue"])
stageRObj2 <- stageR(pScreen = pScreen2, pConfirmation = pConfirmation2, pScreenAdjusted = FALSE)
stageRObj2 <- stageWiseAdjustment(object = stageRObj2, method = "none", alpha = 0.05)

adj_PVals2 <- getAdjustedPValues(stageRObj2, onlySignificantGenes = FALSE, order = FALSE) #returns NA for non-significant gene in pScreen
adj_PVals2 <- as.data.frame(adj_PVals2)

Results_interaction$staged.FDR <- adj_PVals2[rownames(Results_interaction),]$"Interaction"
intDEGs2 <- rownames(na.omit(Results_interaction[Results_interaction$staged.FDR < 0.05, ]))
intDEGs2

```

## D. Comparison of logFCs upon Stress in males and females 

```{r}
merge_M_F <- merge(Results_M, Results_F, by = "row.names", suffix = c(".males", ".females"))

merge_M_F$proteinCoding <- rowData(se)[merge_M_F$Row.names, "proteinCoding"]  

merge_M_F <- merge_M_F[which(merge_M_F$Row.names %in% intDEGs2 & merge_M_F$proteinCoding),] # select protein-coding genes with significant Sex*Stress interaction

sup_fig_coef_d <- ggplot(merge_M_F, aes(logFC.males, logFC.females)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") + 
  geom_abline(slope=1) +
  geom_segment(aes(y=low.females, yend=high.females), color="grey") + 
  geom_segment(aes(x=low.males, xend=high.males), color="grey") + 
  theme_bw() + 
  geom_point() + 
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data=merge_M_F[which(abs(merge_M_F$logFC.males)>0.1 | abs(merge_M_F$logFC.females)>0.1),],
    aes(label=gsub(".+\\.","",Row.names)), max.overlaps = 30, min.segment.length = 0, size=3) +
  labs(x="logFC upon Stress in males", y="logFC upon Stress in females")
sup_fig_coef_d
```

## Top ten genes with a significant interaction and the largest interaction logFC

```{r}
intDF <- Results_interaction[order(abs(Results_interaction$logFC), decreasing = TRUE), ]
top10cand <- head(intDF[which(intDF$staged.FDR < 0.05 & abs(intDF$logFC) > 0.1 & rownames(intDF) %in% cands2),], 10)   # top10 candidates (protein-coding)
gsub(".+\\.","", rownames(top10cand))
```

They are the same genes from the top10 candidates from the reference analysis.

```{r}
brivioGenes <- tools::toTitleCase(tolower(readLines("./datasets/BrivioSexStressGenes2.txt")))
brivioGenes <- getrn(se, brivioGenes)
# check if they overlap with intDEGs:
overlap_gene <- intersect(brivioGenes, intDEGs)
# only Mthfr overlaps

merge_M_F <- merge(Results_M, Results_F, by="row.names", suffix=c(".males",".females"))
merge_M_F_brivio <- merge_M_F[which(merge_M_F$Row.names %in% brivioGenes),]
ct <- cor.test(merge_M_F_brivio$logFC.males, merge_M_F_brivio$logFC.females)
sup_fig_coef_f <- ggplot(merge_M_F_brivio, aes(logFC.males, logFC.females)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") +

  geom_abline(slope = 1) +
  geom_segment(aes(y = low.females, yend = high.females), color = "grey") + 
  geom_segment(aes(x = low.males, xend = high.males), color = "grey") + 
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ 0 + x, method = "lm") + 
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = merge_M_F_brivio[which(abs(merge_M_F_brivio$logFC.males) > 0.25 | abs(merge_M_F_brivio$logFC.females) > 0.25), ],
    aes(label = gsub(".+\\.","",Row.names)), max.overlaps = 30, min.segment.length = 0, size = 3) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = merge_M_F_brivio[which(merge_M_F_brivio$Row.names %in% overlap_gene), ],
    aes(label = gsub(".+\\.","",Row.names)), nudge_x = 0.1, nudge_y = -0.05, max.overlaps = 30, min.segment.length = 0, size = 3) +    
  labs(x = "logFC upon Stress in males", y = "logFC upon Stress in females") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = paste0(" R=", round(ct$estimate, 2), " ***\n"), hjust = 1, vjust = 0)
sup_fig_coef_f
```

## G. Slope regression

In next chunk we ask: does female stress response differ systematically from male response? To answer this, we fit a regression of (female logFC - male logFC) ~ male logFC. We did this in three different gene sets: DEGs from full dataset; balanced DEGs; DEGs from balanced data.

```{r}
# Gene set 1. DEGs from differential analysis of the full dataset, both sexes pooled
merge_M_F <- merge(Results_M, Results_F, by = "row.names", suffix = c(".males",".females"))
m1 <- merge_M_F[which(merge_M_F$Row.names %in% row.names(Results_stress)[which(Results_stress$FDR < 0.05)]),]
# Here this gene set is selected form the analysis which is dominated by males (more samples in the data). 
# So we might have detected more DEGs in males (since we have more power there), which could have led to a bias towards males
# # Thus we also use two other different gene sets.

# Gene set 2. balanced DEGs. 
# Take the same number of top male DEGs as female DEGs, to avoid male-dominated gene selection
balanced_degs <- union(head(row.names(Results_M), sum(Results_F$FDR < 0.05)), row.names(Results_F)[which(Results_F$FDR < 0.05)])  # Since female has less significant genes than male, we extract the number of female DEGs
m2 <- merge_M_F[which(merge_M_F$Row.names %in% balanced_degs),]

# Gene set 3. DEGs from a sex-balanced dataset
# Here we select equal number of males and females, then re-run the differential analysis
# This also removes the power imbalance between sexes
# In this supplement, we only do subsampling once. (See reference analysis for the permutation)

set.seed(1234)
  # In our data, females only exist in two batches: Privitera.E2 and vonZiegler.E3
  # To balance also between different batches, we select 2 ctrl males and 3 stress males from Privitera.E1 batch (the reason to select from this batch is that in MDS plot, this batch is the closest one from batch vonZiegler.E3)
batch_with_both_sexes <- colnames(se)[se$Experiment %in% c("vonZiegler.E3", "Privitera.E2")]
male_ctrl_Privitera.E1 <- sample(colnames(se)[se$Experiment == "Privitera.E1" & se$group == "Male_Ctrl"], 2, replace = FALSE)
male_stress_Privitera.E1 <- sample(colnames(se)[se$Experiment == "Privitera.E1" & se$group == "Male_Stress"], 3, replace = FALSE)
se_sub <- se[,c(batch_with_both_sexes, male_ctrl_Privitera.E1, male_stress_Privitera.E1)]

# filter
dge <- DGEList(assay(se_sub, "counts"))
mm <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group, data=as.data.frame(colData(se_sub)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
# Filter lowly expressed genes
keep <- filterByExpr(dge, mm, min.count = 10)
se_sub <- se_sub[keep, ]

# SVA correction
suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(invisible(capture.output(
    se_sub <- SEtools::svacor(se_sub, ~ 0 + group, n.sv = 2, method = "vst")
  ))))

# DEA
formula <- paste(grep("^SV[0-9]", colnames(colData(se_sub)), value = TRUE), collapse = "+")
formula <- as.formula(paste0("~", formula, "+Sex*Condition"))
mm <- model.matrix(formula, data = as.data.frame(colData(se_sub)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(assay(se_sub)))
dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm)
fit <- glmQLFit(dge, mm, prior.count=0.5)

Results_stress_balanceddata <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, grep("Condition", colnames(mm), value=TRUE)), Inf)) 

m3 <- merge_M_F[merge_M_F$Row.names %in% rownames(Results_stress_balanceddata)[Results_stress_balanceddata$FDR < 0.05], ]
nrow(m3)
# the number of DEGs are decent

# Linear regression on three gene sets: do females respond less than males?
# For each gene set: (femaleLogFC - maleLogFC) ~ maleLogFC
stats <- as.data.frame(t(sapply(list(full = m1, balancedDEGs = m2, balancedData = m3), \(x){
  coef(summary(lm(logFC.females - logFC.males ~ 0 + logFC.males, data = x)))[,-3]
  })))
stats$lab <- paste0(" ", row.names(stats), ": ", round(stats[,1], 3), "; p=", round(stats[,3], 4))

sup_fig_coef_g <- ggplot(m1, aes(logFC.males, logFC.females)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") + 
  theme_bw() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.5, 2.5), ylim = c(-1.5, 2.5)) + 
  geom_abline(slope = 1) + geom_point(alpha = 0.1, size = 0.3) + 
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ 0 + x, method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "logFC upon Stress in males", y = "logFC upon Stress in females") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10)) + 
  annotate("text", label = paste0("\n",paste(stats$lab, collapse = "\n")), x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4)
sup_fig_coef_g
```

# Save Objects for later use

```{r}
# save the result
stress_degs_MFunion <- union(M_signif, F_signif) 
stressed_animals <- se[,se$Condition == "Stress"]$SampleName
mean_log2fc <- rowMeans(assay(se, "log2FC")[stress_degs_MFunion, stressed_animals])
filtered_stress_degs_MFunion <- mean_log2fc[abs(mean_log2fc) > 0.1]

DEGs <- list(
  MF_union_stress_degs = stress_degs_MFunion,
  MF_stress_degs_filtered = filtered_stress_degs_MFunion,
  Interaction_degs_stageR_by_allResults = intDEGs, 
  Interaction_degs_stageR_by_subsetResults = intDEGs2)

coef_obj = list(se = se, 
                   DEGs = DEGs,
                   edgeR = Results)
saveRDS(coef_obj, "./objects/coef_obj.rds")
```
